correctness.rationale: For each nonzero residue r modulo n, the increments from n+1 and n+2 must sum to at least r, so at least ceil(r/2) such generators are needed; that many attain the increment r. The resulting genus is h^2 for n=2h and h(h+1) for n=2h+1. In the even case, for any prime p dividing an admissible modulus, p divides h, and the gap polynomial at a primitive p-th root is nonzero (including p=2). In the odd case I checked the finite geometric sums, their factorization under genus divisibility, and the unit-circle nonvanishing of the remaining quadratic. The separately grouped sum at order three is nonzero when 3 divides h. Testing all nonidentity roots, rather than only a primitive root, gives exactly the claimed exclusion when m divides h and 3 divides m. The n=3 endpoint is included. An independent direct-membership dynamic program agreed for 2,242 pairs, 3 <= n <= 40 and 2 <= m <= 60; this is corroboration, not the proof. The supplied verifier was inspected but not run.
residual_risks: No formal verification or external attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: A natural family of width-two semigroups has a complete modular gap classification beyond parity. It tells a reader exactly which divisors of the genus give equality, including the nontrivial obstruction at order three and the failure of mixed factors from consecutive h and h+1. These are useful distinctions not read off from the genus or the generator parity.
residual_risks: The result does not classify wider generator intervals or factorization lengths.
